paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The same God who said He had resolved to bring disaster did not stay stuck there. He says, "so now I have resolved to do good again to Jerusalem and Judah. Do not be afraid." (Zechariah 8:14-15) And it all starts with Him saying, "I am jealous for Zion with great zeal." (Zechariah 8:2) That is love that refuses to give up, and it's the kind of love I needed in that drawer!

Then God asks the question that should stop us all: "If this is impossible in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be impossible in My eyes?" (Zechariah 8:6) Friend, some days you look at your life and say, "No way that gets fixed." God's answer is that your doubt isn't the measuring stick. He also tells them what to do while they wait: "Let your hands be strong," and "Speak truth to one another." (Zechariah 8:13, 16) You don't have to see the whole finished cookie box to keep pressing the dough!

And look where the promise lands. The gloomy fasts become "times of joy and gladness, cheerful feasts," and people from the nations say, "Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you." (Zechariah 8:19, 23) So whatever feels heavy in your life right now, God can turn it into joy, and the way you live can point folks straight to Him. That's why I keep my ovens ready, friend. The story isn't over!
